title: Compression Pipeline Audit — Universal Scheduler Phase 6A

summary.migration_verdict: cleanest fit — file-task model, module-level worker, disjoint outputs, no merge step

entry_points.invoked_by: manual per docs/huggingface_release_pipeline.md; tests/test_release_pipeline.py (4 compression tests); no production callers

cli_flags.meaning: raw parallel worker count (old audit said 1 — stale; on-disk default is 2)
list shards + preview category, write nothing
skip shards whose output files exist and decompress OK

worker.name: _route_shard
behavior: route each record by rec['category'] (NOT filename — mixed shards exist)
close writers, then verify in same worker (count_jsonl_zst + sha256_file)
worker.return_shape: {input, input_bytes, input_records, by_category, verified, errors, elapsed_s}

executor.sequential_fallback: workers <= 1 -> sequential loop, same worker fn
executor.completion: as_completed then re-sorted by input name

execution_model.parallelization_safety: each shard writes its own {category}/{stem}.jsonl.zst files; no two workers touch the same output file

merge_order_guarantees.report_aggregation: sorted(results, key=lambda x: x['input']) — shard filename order
merge_order_guarantees.zstd_determinism: single-threaded frames, fixed level -> byte-deterministic for identical input+level

retry_resume.resume: planner-time disk scan (--skip-existing): skip shard if ANY category output exists AND all found files decompress OK
resume_failure_modes: partial-output shard (crash wrote category A not B) is NOT detected — A's file exists so shard skipped -> silent partial output
corrupt-but-countable file (count >= 0, wrong records) treated as OK

integrity.in_worker_verification: decompress + count + sha256 per output file
integrity.downstream: sha256s feed generate_checksums.py / verify_release.py (separate tools, out of scope)

resource_usage.cpu: raw CLI int (default 2), no caps, no adaptive sizing
resource_usage.ram: O(1) streaming per worker + zstd frame buffers; no RAM-aware limit
resource_usage.disk: writes ~1/3 raw input; docs warn ensure free space >= source size; no disk check in code

becomes_scheduler_task: one file task per shard; worker compress_task(task) wraps _route_shard verbatim
worker raises when errors non-empty OR any verified.ok False (scheduler retry needs exception)
worker resolution via resolve_worker_count('release') / safe_worker_limit(); --workers kept as CLI override
remains_serialized: planner: glob + sort shards, --skip-existing disk scan, dry-run listing
finalize single writer: aggregation sorted by task_id, compression_report.json + statistics.json writes, exit-code decision
registry_state: task_id, status, attempt, timestamp, error, record_count telemetry
task_id MUST embed release: compress:{release}:{shard_stem} — registry is repo-global; bare compress:{shard} collides across releases
migration_boundary.cannot_parallelize: nothing at shard level (disjoint outputs); only report aggregation order must stay deterministic (serialized finalize)

config.py.note: resolve_worker_count('release') reads release.compress_workers (DEFAULTS 'auto'; YAML has no release section — verified on disk)

resource.py.note: safe_worker_limit fits CPU-bound zstd; disk_free() reporting-only — R2 from 5E, re-evaluate for disk-heavy compression

models.py.note: Task/TaskResult fit file tasks; extra={out_root, level}

planner.py.note: file_tasks() -> one Task per shard; task_id source:operation:name matches compress:{release}:{stem}

scheduler.py.note: bounded submission, retry <= max_retries, resume-skip, deterministic sort, in-run dedupe; _backpressure() dead-code is scheduler-wide cleanup, out of scope

monitor.py.note: Monitor writes reports/performance/compression_scheduler_report.json; not required for correctness

findings.finding: No registry / no task-state resume; --skip-existing is a disk heuristic that can silently accept partial output after crash
findings.impact: Migration closes via per-shard task completion + lease re-claim

findings.finding: Verification failure is non-retryable (hard exit 1); worker records ok=False instead of raising
findings.impact: Migration: worker raises -> scheduler retry; exit 1 preserved on terminal failure

findings.finding: Worker count is raw CLI int (default 2), no RAM/CPU caps; uneven shards idle workers
Zero disk-awareness while compression is disk-heavy (docs: keep free space >= source size)
findings.impact: Keep --workers 1 guidance; optional pre-flight disk_free() check in finalize (design decision)

findings.finding: task_id must embed release tag or global registry collides across releases
Registry record_count telemetry: _record_count() looks for record_count/total/classified/processed; worker returns input_records -> 0
findings.impact: Add 'total' alias in worker result payload

findings.finding: --skip-existing semantics vs registry resume divergence (file deleted but task completed)
findings.impact: Keep flag as planner-time disk check; registry resume additional; verify_release catches missing files downstream

findings.finding: Old atlas_parallelism_audit.md says worker default 1 — stale; on-disk default is 2

decisions_needed.question: Registry stage key
decisions_needed.recommendation: compression — isolates from Phase 7 release tools; task_ids already carry operation prefix for future sharing

decisions_needed.question: --skip-existing mapping
options: keep as planner-time disk check layered on registry resume
decisions_needed.recommendation: keep flag as disk check + registry resume (belt-and-suspenders, preserves today's flag contract)

decisions_needed.question: Worker cap
options: leave release.compress_workers at 'auto' (safe limit — behavior change from default 2)
decisions_needed.recommendation: pin modest default in YAML at implementation time; document ATLAS_WORKERS_RELEASE / --workers for constrained machines

decisions_needed.question: Failure semantics
decisions_needed.recommendation: worker raises (retryable); exit 1 preserved on terminal failure
